The court itself noted that the accused No. 1 company (Nisarag Forests (I) Ltd.) was under liquidation, and that prima facie there was no material on record showing complaints from investors that they had not been refunded [clf-pvstegqbqv7bpznmxxjd9tej#42].

- Amount collected from investors: Rs. 10.66 crores
- Amount refunded to investors: Rs. 39 lakh (Rs. 0.39 crore)
- Amount remaining unrefunded: Rs. 10.66 crores - Rs. 0.39 crore = approximately Rs. 10.27 crores

The Ld. SPP Ms. Sabiha Ansari submitted that "the accused have collected amount of Rs.10.66 crores from the investors out of which only 39 lakh were refunded to the investors. Huge amount is remain to be refunded to the investors at large."

So the answer is approximately Rs. 10.27 crores (Rs. 10.66 crores - Rs. 0.39 crore) remained unrefunded. The court itself characterizes this as a "huge amount" remaining to be refunded.

Let me write the final answer now.

In SEBI Spl Case No. 259/14 (judgment dated 16.10.2024, delivered by SEBI Special Judge R. M. Jadhav at the City Civil & Sessions Court, Greater Bombay), the figures placed before the court by the Ld. SPP Ms. Sabiha Ansari were:

- **Amount remaining unrefunded:** approximately **Rs. 10.27 crores** (Rs. 10.66 crore − Rs. 0.39 crore)

Huge amount is remain to be refunded to the investors at large." [clf-pvstegqbqv7bpznmxxjd9tej#40][clf-pvstegqbqv7bpznmxxjd9tej#41]
